incident-bot: [INCIDENT] p99 latency spike detected in us-east-1 · /v1/stream/generate · streaming stalls observed · SLO burn: p99 > 5s for last 5m · tracking id=inc-1759741123 :rotating_light:
Priya K: Acked. I'm oncall. Looking at dashboards now. Can someone paste the p95/p99 numbers?
Dan: p95 jumped from ~380ms -> 1.1s over last 10m. p99 from ~1.2s -> ~6.4s. Streaming stall counts up ~7% of streams (clients reporting stalled chunks).
Alice: Seeing a big drop in prefix cache hit rate for pf-v3 namespace, hitrate down from 89% -> 21% after the prefix-hash rollout at 03:02 UTC. Metric: cache.prefix_hitrate{namespace=pf-v3} ~0.21.
Samir: Confirmed. KV namespace rekey happened 03:02 UTC as part of rollout. Seems like many keys not matching new salt -> massive cold reads -> paging pressure -> tail latency.
Priya K: Good call. Customer impact? Any 5xxs or aborted connections?
Dan: No spike in 5xxs in logs. Mostly delayed tokens and increased stream-inactivity timeouts (clients eventually reconnect). Top symptom: long initial token delay (head), then either slow stream or stall.
Alice: Paging queues for backend-pagers are spiking. Avg queue depth 40 -> 220 in us-east-1. Paging worker CPU ~95% on some shards.
infra-bot: Autoscaling triggered +2 paging workers in us-east-1 but queue is still high.
Priya K: Immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) throttle non-critical streaming routes to reduce pressure, 2) increase cache TTLs temporarily to favour existing items, 3) run targeted warmup for pf-v3 namespace, 4) if safe, revert prefix-hash rollout to previous salt.
Samir: I can run a warmup backfill. Proposed command:```bash
# warm cache for pf-v3, parallel across 12 shards
./tools/warm_prefetch_cache --namespace pf-v3 --shards 12 --parallel 48 --batch 100
```
Alice: Also bumping cache TTL via runtime config: set runtime.cache.ttl.pf-v3 = 300 (seconds) to reduce churn. I'll push to canary in us-east-1 first.
Dan: Throttle plan: add route rule to rate-limit /v1/stream/generate for non-Sentry customers to 10rps for next 15m. Will patch ingress with quick rule.
Priya K: Runbook item: If rollback needed, revert key in config-store:```bash
# revert salt to previous value
kubectl -n config apply -f configs/prefix-salt-prev.yaml
```Samir: Rolling back salt is heavy — will cause its own cache churn. Prefer warmup + TTL bump + scaling while we evaluate.
Alice: I'll scale paging workers to 25 replicas to give breathing room:```bash
kubectl scale deploy/backing-pagers -n production --replicas=25
```
Dan: Kicking off warmup now. I'll monitor queue depth and p99. Priya, please own on-call comms and customer updates.
Priya K: Noted. Sending initial customer notice to growth & support: short blurb explaining increased latency and that we're mitigating; will share timeline when we have more.
incident-bot: Action items assigned: Samir (warmup), Alice (TTL canary + scale), Dan (throttle + monitor), Priya (customer comms & coordination).
Samir: Warmup started @ 1759741600. Running across 12 shards. ETA ~ 12m for first pass.
Dan: After warmup started p99 trending down: 6.4s -> 3.2s in last 6m. queue depth down ~220 -> 140. Still above baseline.
Alice: Canary TTL bump in us-east-1 applied. Observing no regressions. If stable in 5m, I'll roll region-wide.
Priya K: Customer impact update: roughly ~4-8% of streaming requests experienced noticeable stalls (measured by client-side rebuffering). No confirmed customer-facing errors, but latency SLO is degraded. Support notified top 10 enterprise customers.
Samir: Warmup pass complete @ 1759742350. Cache hitrate for pf-v3 up from 21% -> 68%. Paging queue continuing to fall.
Dan: p99 now ~1.4s, p95 ~520ms. Streaming stall reports down to ~1.2%. Good trend.
Alice: Rolling TTL region-wide now. Also left a short cleanup job to expire stale keys older than 24h to avoid slow growth.
Priya K: Next steps: 1) keep warmup running until hitrate >80% for 30m, 2) monitor p99 <1.0s target, 3) keep throttles for 30m and re-evaluate, 4) do not revert salt without full runbook signoff.
Dan: Agreed. I'll keep watch and escalate if p99 climbs.
Maya: I'll take handoff at 1759744800. Before I take it, what's open for me?
Priya K: Handoff checklist for Maya: 1) Ensure warmup is still running and hitrate trending up, 2) Confirm paging queue < 60, 3) Confirm p99 < 1.2s for 20m, 4) Keep TTL bump live for 1h then evaluate rollback to normal, 5) Pause any rollout or rekey work until we finish postmortem.
Maya: Got it. I'll be on for the next shift. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated (partial) · monitoring for regression · assigned: Maya (oncall next). Reference inc-1759741123 for postmortem creation.
Priya K: Handoff done. Leaving notes in incident tracker and Jira. I'll start draft postmortem with timeline and mitigation details.
Samir: Leaving logs & warmup report in S3: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/1759741123/warmup-report.json
Priya K: Closing chat for now. If anything spikes, ping @Priya K or @Maya. Thanks all for fast response. :pray:
